name: Valley terraces
kicker: Rice terraces on a limestone valley
summary: Give the morning to the terrace walls, with the limestone ridge behind the crop. Stay if that valley is the trip. Go to Mai Chau for Bản Lác, and to Ninh Binh for the boats. Late May to early June is green young rice on the conservation pages and on Vietnam Tourism. September and October are gold on those pages. A provincial trekking note calls both windows golden. No terrace ticket was printed. The hour is check on arrival.
getThere: From a stilt house at Bản Đôn, the fields are the view.
heroCaption: Terrace walls holding water, with the limestone ridge behind

notice.title: May is the green crop
notice.body: Come in late May for green young rice. September and October are the gold window on the conservation pages and on Vietnam Tourism. A provincial trekking note calls both windows golden.

body: Walk the edges of the terraces in the morning. The conservation pages and Vietnam Tourism put green young rice in late May to early June, and ripe gold in September and October. A provincial trekking note calls both of those windows ripe and golden, so a May field is not a gold field on those two pages. Vietnam Tourism also names bamboo water wheels that lift stream water onto the fields, and calls them a Thai marker. They are scattered. No single wheel has an address on that page.

The fields are the view from a stilt house if you sleep at Bản Đôn, in old Thành Lâm, now inside xã Pù Luông. Bản Hiêu and the hamlets Son, Bá, and Mười sit in xã Cổ Lũng. A fixed hour for the fields was not printed. Check on arrival. There is no terrace ticket on the conservation pages or on Vietnam Tourism. The fee is check on arrival.

figures.caption: Two people walking the rice terraces, with the limestone ridge behind
figures.alt: Two people on a path through rice terraces, limestone hills behind them in Pu Luong

gettingThere: The terraces are the valley floor and the lower slopes, especially around Bản Đôn and on the Hiêu side. If you sleep at Bản Đôn, the fields are the view from the house. A bicycle is what Vietnam Tourism says visitors are offered on the valley road, with steeper lanes if you want them. Homestays often lend a bicycle without a charge. That often is one account. The charge is check on arrival.

legs.heading: From Bản Đôn
legs.body: On foot from the house. The fields start at the foot of the hill. A minute count for that walk was not printed. Check on arrival.

legs.heading: From Hanoi
legs.body: By road. The conservation pages print about 210 km. Vietnam Tourism prints about 160 km southwest, and a limousine of about 4.5 hours from Giáp Bát or Mỹ Đình. No minute count sits beside either kilometer. A car or a motorbike hired in Hanoi is the usual road.

closed: No weekly closing day was printed. Check on arrival.
